newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil plans onshore Norway pipeline link.
newsitem.headline: Statoil plans onshore Norway pipeline link.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Thursday it had unveiled plans to lay pipelines to link the gas treatment plant at Kollsnes outside Bergen to the Sture crude oil terminal and the Mongstad refinery.
The state-owned oil company operates Kollsnes and Mongstad, while Norsk Hydro is responsible for Sture. Mongstad is about 30 kilometres from Kollsnes/Sture.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said that when Norsk Hydro's Oseberg field begins producing gas in 1999, the plans call for unstabilised crude to be piped through the existing oil line to Sture.
A stabilisation facility at the terminal will strip natural gas liquids (NGLs) from this flow, and these NGLs could be piped on to Mongstad for processing, it said.
The same oil line could also carry condensate from Kollsnes to Mongstad, where a new plant is planned to produce propane, butane and naphtha.
The naphtha would be blended with oil products from the refinery, while the other NGLs would be sold on the open market, Statoil said.
It said it estimated the cost of the pipelines and the planned NGL plant at Mongstad at 1.5 billion crowns. It said the plans were passed to partners last week.
